## Highlights

- See every registered scheduler in All Systems, search across them, and take explicit target-checked actions without implying shared execution, failover, or clustering.
- Use least-authority local and remote MCP actions, named grants, and bounded audit evidence. Agent access and network listeners remain opt-in.
- Export, inspect, and apply portable automation bundles with selected-target compatibility checks and redacted source and notification policy intent.
- Configure durable webhook conditions for failures, recovery, start problems, long runs, and healthy-presence heartbeats; SMTP email remains future work.
- Opt into filterable native desktop popups for new task outcomes and alerts on supported Windows, macOS, and Linux desktop sessions. They require the GUI to be running; webhooks remain the unattended delivery path.
- Use user-session Windows tray and Linux status indicators for local daemon visibility and protected service controls even when the GUI is closed. Exact-candidate attended Windows checks remain untested under a maintainer-authorized waiver; automated CI, staging, candidate identity, and checksums remain required. This release does not claim complete native Windows qualification.

Read the [full changelog](https://github.com/shruggietech/go-schedule/blob/v1.5.0/CHANGELOG.md#150---2026-09-23) for every change.
